description.value: The Gold Bridge Library is a branch of the Lillooet Area Library Association, a community non-profit serving the small and isolated Bridge River Valley. It offers internet access and a community room in a part of BC where services are scarce. For cyclists riding the Hurley Forest Service Road or exploring the Bralorne area, the branch represents a rare digital lifeline in an otherwise off-grid landscape.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms the Lillooet Area Library Association actively operates branches in Lillooet, Gold Bridge, and Shalalth; the OSM record tags this specific Gold Bridge location. OSM includes internet_access=wlan and the website lists 'Computers & Internet' as an in-library service, supporting Wi-Fi as true. No cycling-specific amenities — bike parking, washrooms, or water refill — are mentioned on the website or in OSM tags for this branch, so all three required criteria remain null.
concerns: Website footer displays phone 250-256-7944 and email director@lillooetlibrary.ca, which appear to belong to the main Lillooet branch; OSM phone +1-250-238-2521 and email jean@lillooetlibrary.ca are likely Gold Bridge-specific but cannot be confirmed from the website.
The LALA website covers all three branches without branch-specific detail pages, making it impossible to verify amenities unique to the Gold Bridge location.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Gold Bridge is a remote community on a popular cycling route and a library with Wi-Fi has real potential value to touring cyclists, but none of the three required criteria (bike parking, water, washrooms) can be confirmed from available evidence; direct contact or a site visit is needed before listing.
enrichment_extras.notes: Gold Bridge sits at the end of the Hurley FSR, a well-known gravel cycling corridor linking Pemberton to the Bridge River Valley. Even a minimal confirmed amenity set (washrooms + water) would make this a worthwhile listing given the scarcity of services in the area.

provenance.category_correction_reason: A public library branch is more accurately a service stop than an attraction; consider recategorizing as 'Services' if that category exists in the WWC schema.

wow_evidence: Small community library; ordinary intrinsic delight.
blurb: Community library with internet access in the remote Bridge River Valley.
